test_title: PYST 1: SSC Stenographer - English (Held on: 11 Nov 2021 Shift 1 )
subject: english
question:
**Select the correct direct narration of the given sentence.** 

I told my driver that it was raining heavily and requested him to drive slowly.

options.text: “It is raining heavily,” I told my driver and asked, “Would you drive slowly?"
“It is raining heavily. Please drive slowly,” I said to my driver.
I said to my driver, “It was raining heavily. Can you please drive slowly?”
I told my driver, “It has been raining heavily and I am requesting to drive slowly."

solution:
The correct answer is: **“It is raining heavily. Please drive slowly,” I said to my driver.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **in****direct **speech and we need to convert it into a direct speech.
 
• The given sentence is also an imperative sentence.
 
• We follow these rules in Direct-Indirect speech for an imperative sentence:
 
 
• The sense of command, **order, advise, and request is implied** in the reported clause of the sentence. We have to change the reporting verb in accordance with the mood of the sentence. 
 
• **Told **is used as reporting verb instead of say, tell, say to. 
 
• In the imperative sentence the reporting verb **‘said’, ‘said to’, ‘told’** changes to **advised, command, requested, ordered,** etc. depending on the mood of the sentence. 
 
• Imperative sentence changes to statement form [direct to indirect speech]
 
• The conjunction ‘that’ is used to connect reporting and reported clause.
 
 
 
• Example -* **He said to Ranju, “Please, bring a glass of water.” (Direct)*

* He requested Ranju to bring a glass of water. (Indirect)*

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2.

The Direct sentence is: *“It is raining heavily. Please drive slowly,” I said to my driver.*
